pk.context: 100 mg single oral dose, healthy adults

clues.title: Approval
clues.text: Approved by FDA in October 2006 as film-coated tablets for oral use, in 25, 50 and 100 mg strengths.

clues.title: Sponsor and dosing
clues.text: Held by Merck Sharp & Dohme. Dosed once daily, with or without food.

clues.title: Class
clues.text: A dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4) inhibitor. It does not inhibit DPP-8 or DPP-9 at concentrations near therapeutic doses.

clues.title: Mechanism
clues.text: Slows inactivation of the incretins GLP-1 and GIP, increasing insulin release and lowering glucagon in a glucose-dependent manner.

clues.title: Drug substance
clues.text: A phosphate monohydrate salt, MW 523.32, of a base holding six fluorine atoms, C₁₆H₁₅F₆N₅O. A white to off-white, non-hygroscopic powder soluble in water.

clues.title: Tablets
clues.text: Round film-coated tablets colored with iron oxides and debossed with a number: pink at 25 mg, light beige at 50 mg, beige at 100 mg.

clues.title: Absorption
clues.text: Absolute bioavailability is about 87% and a high-fat meal has no effect. Median Tmax is 1 to 4 hours; only 38% is bound to plasma protein.

clues.title: Elimination
clues.text: About 79% is excreted unchanged in urine, with active tubular secretion via OAT3. Minor metabolism is mostly CYP3A4. Below an eGFR of 45 the dose is reduced.

clues.title: Warnings
clues.text: Warnings include pancreatitis, heart failure, acute renal failure, severe arthralgia and bullous pemphigoid. The only contraindication is serious hypersensitivity.

clues.title: Indication
clues.text: An adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes. Not for type 1 diabetes.
